status_policy.promotion_policy: A rule is never promoted from proposal or committee review to adopted, in-force or applicable by model inference. rules.title: EU Emissions Trading System maritime transport coverage
rules.instrument: Directive 2003/87/EC as amended, including Directive (EU) 2023/959 and maritime implementing provisions
rules.revision_or_resolution: Consolidated text and current Commission guidance must be consulted

applicability.ship_scope: Since 2024: cargo and passenger ships ≥5,000 GT; from 2027: offshore ships ≥5,000 GT. MRV scope differs and includes additional 400–5,000 GT offshore/general cargo ships from 2025.
applicability.geographic_scope: EU/EEA port emissions and voyages with EU port calls, as defined in current law.
applicability.voyage_scope: 100% coverage for voyages between EU ports and emissions within EU ports; 50% coverage for voyages with one end outside the EU, subject to the legal rules.
conditions: The EU ETS is flag-neutral and route-based.
100% of emissions for eligible voyages between EU/EEA ports and 100% of eligible emissions within EU/EEA ports.
50% of eligible emissions for voyages between an EU/EEA port and a non-EU/EEA port.
CH4 and N2O are included in ETS maritime scope from emissions year 2026.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Applicability, responsible company, ship scope, exemptions and voyage classification must be resolved from legal text and verified facts.

output_scope: EU ETS covered CH4 emissions from 2026
EU ETS covered N2O emissions from 2026

calculation_contract.formula_or_method: Aggregate gas-specific emissions by eligible voyage/port segment and reporting year, applying the legally defined coverage share and surrender phase-in. Preserve each gas and the applicable GWP/calculation method.

70% of emissions from 2025 to be covered by allowances surrendered in 2026.

limitations: Port approach/departure outside port of call is part of the voyage, not within-port emissions.

rules.title: EU Monitoring, Reporting and Verification of maritime transport emissions
rules.revision_or_resolution: Consolidated EU MRV Maritime Regulation and applicable implementing acts

applicability.ship_scope: From 2024: cargo and passenger ships ≥5,000 GT; from 2025 reporting period: offshore ships ≥5,000 GT and offshore/general cargo ships ≥400 GT and <5,000 GT, subject to detailed legal scope and exclusions.
applicability.geographic_scope: Voyages to, from and between EU/EEA ports and emissions within ports under the MRV Maritime Regulation's scope.
applicability.voyage_scope: Monitoring, reporting and verification of gas-specific ship emissions and related activity data for each reporting period; do not confuse the MRV scope with EU ETS allowance coverage.
conditions: CO2 has been monitored/reported under EU MRV since 2018.
CH4 and N2O are within EU MRV monitoring/reporting from emissions year 2024.
Annual reporting follows the statutory reporting period and voyage/port definitions.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Exact ship scope, monitoring plan, port-call definition, exclusions and verifier requirements must be resolved under the consolidated regulation and implementing acts.
MRV reporting coverage does not mean all reported gases are in EU ETS surrender scope in the same year.

calculation_contract.formula_or_method: Monitor and aggregate ship emissions and activity data using the prescribed MRV monitoring plan and approved method. Preserve CO2, CH4 and N2O as separate gases and bind to the relevant reporting year and verifier status.

limitations: Subject to ship and reporting scope under the regulation.
Gas included in the MRV monitoring/reporting scope from 2024.
Gas included in the MRV monitoring/reporting scope from 2024.
MRV is a monitoring/reporting/verification obligation, not an allowance surrender requirement.
MRV gas coverage and EU ETS gas coverage have different start years; do not reuse one rule for both.

rules.title: North-East Atlantic NOx ECA — Tier III new-ship applicability

applicability.ship_scope: Ships operating in the designated North-East Atlantic NOx ECA, with relevant marine diesel engines of more than 130 kW and qualifying construction/delivery dates.
applicability.geographic_scope: Exclusive economic zones and territorial seas extending up to 200 nautical miles from baselines of Greenland, Iceland, the Faroe Islands, Ireland, the mainland United Kingdom, France, Spain and Portugal, as described in the MEPC 84 outcome; authoritative adopted coordinates/chart data are still required.

ship_construction_triggers.meaning: Building contract placed on or after 1 January 2027.
Where no building contract exists, keel laid or similar stage of construction on or after 1 July 2027.
Ship delivered on or after 1 January 2031.

conditions: The amendment enters into force on 1 September 2027.
Tier III applicability requires ECA operation, a relevant marine diesel engine above 130 kW and at least one alternative construction/delivery trigger.
Construction/delivery triggers are alternatives, not cumulative.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Do not apply Tier III to every existing ship merely because it enters the ECA.

Official adopted ECA polygon coordinates are still required for geospatial classification.

calculation_contract.formula_or_method: Applicable only when the ship operates inside the official ECA on or after 2027-09-01, a relevant marine diesel engine is >130 kW, and at least one alternative build/delivery trigger is satisfied. rules.title: North-East Atlantic SOx/PM ECA — 0.10% fuel sulphur limit

applicability.ship_scope: Ships subject to MARPOL Annex VI regulation 14 fuel-sulphur requirements while operating within the designated North-East Atlantic SOx ECA.
applicability.geographic_scope: Exclusive economic zones and territorial seas extending up to 200 nautical miles from baselines of Greenland, Iceland, the Faroe Islands, Ireland, the mainland United Kingdom, France, Spain and Portugal, as described in the MEPC 84 outcome; authoritative adopted coordinates/chart data are still required.
applicability.voyage_scope: Use of fuel oil on operational/voyage segments within the ECA on or after 1 September 2028.

rules.title: Maritime MRV and FuelEU streamlining proposal — COM(2026) 620
rules.instrument: Proposal for a Regulation amending Regulations (EU) 2015/757 and (EU) 2023/1805

applicability.ship_scope: Proposed changes to maritime MRV and FuelEU monitoring/reporting; proposal would extend MRV to additional ship categories including oil/chemical/gas/LNG tankers, Ro-Pax and passenger ships 400–5,000 GT from 2029, subject to final text.
applicability.geographic_scope: EU/EEA maritime MRV and FuelEU scope as defined by adopted legislation.
applicability.voyage_scope: Scenario analysis only until the regulation is adopted and applicable.
conditions: Proposal seeks one aligned MRV system for GHG emissions, well-to-wake emissions and energy used on board, with a single monitoring plan and a single ship report.
Proposed definition of energy used on board is GJ for propulsion and onboard equipment at sea or at berth.
Proposed substitute energy sources include renewable energy generated on board, onshore power supply and wind-assisted propulsion systems.
Proposed definition of wind-assisted propulsion includes partial or full propulsion by wind energy harnessed through rotor sails, kites, hard/rigid sails, soft sails, suction wings or turbines.

Proposed monitoring method counts fuel use from all fuel consumers and energy from substitute sources; wind energy amount is to use international standards and certification references specified in future Commission implementing acts.
Proposal text requires transparent, reproducible monitoring records and proposes at least 10 years of data retention.
exclusions_or_unknowns: European Parliament procedure 2026/0210(COD) status is awaiting committee decision in the 10 November 2026 snapshot.
The proposal itself does not specify the wind-energy calculation standard/certification method; future implementing acts are contemplated.
This is not an adopted rule and does not establish a current legal WAPS energy-accounting formula.
Do not equate modelled avoided fuel or shaft-energy displacement with regulatory wind-energy-used values without the future method.

limitations: Proposal published 17 July 2026; refresh as the ordinary legislative procedure progresses.
Standards/certification for wind-energy amount are future implementing acts and are not supplied by this record.
Do not infer that the proposal or its future methodology is in force.

rules.title: FuelEU Maritime Article 6 zero-emission-at-berth requirement for eligible containerships and passenger ships
rules.revision_or_resolution: Use consolidated Regulation and current Commission guidance

applicability.ship_scope: Passenger ships and ships carrying exclusively containers, within Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 vessel/company/GT scope. The zero-emission-at-berth requirement does not automatically apply to general-cargo or mixed-cargo ships.
applicability.geographic_scope: EU ports covered by AFIR Article 9 from 1 January 2030; all other EU ports that develop OPS facilities from 1 January 2035, subject to Article 6 and the current Regulation.
applicability.voyage_scope: Ships at berth, moored to the quayside, for the period and conditions set out in FuelEU Maritime Article 6.
conditions: The ship categories in scope are passenger ships and ships carrying exclusively containers, within the Regulation's applicable gross-tonnage and company scope.

From 1 January 2030, eligible ships at berth in AFIR Article 9 covered ports must connect to OPS and use it for all electrical power demand at berth, or use an applicable zero-emission technology, subject to exceptions.
From 1 January 2035, the same obligation applies in other ports that develop OPS facilities.
From 1 January 2030 through 31 December 2034, Member States may extend the obligation in specified circumstances to ports/parts of ports not covered by AFIR Article 9.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Do not apply automatically to general cargo or mixed-use/mixed-cargo vessels.
Check the consolidated Regulation's ship scope, gross tonnage, exceptions, port status and any Member-State early application.
An AFIR infrastructure obligation does not prove that a specific berth has live, compatible or reserved OPS power.

output_scope: OPS connection or zero-emission technology requirement

calculation_contract.formula_or_method: Resolve ship type (passenger or exclusively container), gross tonnage, company/voyage scope, berth status, port AFIR Article 9 coverage or OPS-equipment status, effective date and exceptions. Do not infer a mandate for general-cargo or mixed-cargo vessels.

limitations: This rule record is a machine-readable interpretation aid and not a legal opinion or verifier statement.
Use consolidated Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, applicable amendments, AFIR status and Member-State implementation for actual determinations.
